Day by day

The route

Check items off as you go; progress stays saved on this device. The 7th and 8th stay deliberately light after work.

Tuesday06October
Arrival night

Touch down, check in, sleep

  • Arrive in Thessaloniki at approximately 23:00.
  • Use a pre-booked transfer or official taxi; late-night public transport may be limited.
  • Stay near Aristotelous Square, Agia Sofia or the waterfront for an easy walking base.
Keep it simple: tell the hotel about the late arrival and confirm reception or self-check-in in advance.
Wednesday07October
Work 09:00–19:00 · light evening

Dinner and a waterfront reset

  • Finish work and have a quiet halal dinner near the center—HAYAT Mikrí Póli is a practical first option.
  • Take an easy, flat stroll from the White Tower along the illuminated waterfront.
  • Turn back whenever energy dips; tonight is for settling in, not ticking off sights.
Open gentle evening route ↗
Thursday08October
Work 09:00–19:00 · light evening

A calm evening in the old center

  • After work, walk through Aristotelous Square and along the waterfront promenade.
  • Choose a simple halal Turkish meal at Pites tis Polis, or vegetarian/seafood after confirming ingredients and shared-grill practices.
  • Optional short loop past the Rotunda exterior and Arch of Galerius; save all formal visits for Friday.
Open optional evening route ↗
No nightlife needed: these stops are public squares, monuments and promenades; the evening can end immediately after dinner.
Friday09October
Full day · heritage focus · uphill

Ottoman Thessaloniki and Ano Poli

  • Start at Yeni Camii, then walk to the Rotunda and its surviving Ottoman minaret.
  • Continue through the center to Bey Hamam, Hamza Bey Mosque and Alaca Imaret.
  • Pause for Friday prayer if you have confirmed a suitable local prayer space; the historic mosques are generally not regular places of worship.
  • After a halal lunch, take a taxi or bus uphill to Heptapyrgion and walk down through Ano Poli past Musa Baba’s türbe and old fountains.
  • Optional Atatürk House Museum if it has reopened; otherwise enjoy a quiet tea and an early evening.
Open heritage route ↗
Access note: Yeni Camii and Alaca Imaret often open only for exhibitions. Hamza Bey Mosque has been under restoration; treat an interior visit as a bonus.
Saturday10October
Museum morning · transfer afternoon

One museum, then Thessaloniki → Athens

  • Choose one: Museum of Byzantine Culture or the Archaeological Museum. Keep luggage at the hotel.
  • Target an afternoon train or flight; book only after the operator publishes the confirmed October schedule.
  • Check in around Monastiraki, Syntagma or Koukaki for easy airport and sightseeing connections.
  • Have a quiet halal dinner near the hotel; add a short Plaka or Monastiraki walk only if energy allows.
Recommendation: the direct train is city-center to city-center; flying is the backup. Recheck for engineering works or timetable changes before purchase.
Sunday11October
Full day · timed entry

Classical Athens

  • Book the Acropolis for the first available morning slot; enter before the larger crowds.
  • Acropolis Museum, then a halal or vegetarian lunch after confirming ingredients.
  • Walk via Plaka and the Roman Agora to Monastiraki.
  • Finish with Syntagma and the National Garden, or Lycabettus Hill according to energy.
  • Pack tonight and confirm the airport transfer.
Open Athens route ↗
Monday12October
Departure morning

Athens airport

  • Leave central Athens roughly 3 hours before an international flight, plus transfer time.
  • For a very early flight, pre-book a taxi; metro service may not yet be running.
  • Check out and depart Athens.
Ottoman & Muslim heritage

Six essential remains

Most are historic monuments or exhibition venues rather than active mosques. Always verify same-day access.

01

Bey Hamam

Built in 1444 by Sultan Murad II—the city’s earliest Ottoman public building and its great surviving double bath.

Official guide ↗
02

Alaca Imaret

A 1484 mosque and charitable complex, recognizable by its twin domes; now a municipal exhibition space.

Visitor information ↗
03

Yeni Camii

Vitaliano Poselli’s 1902 mosque for the Dönme community, blending Islamic and European architectural languages.

City overview ↗
04

Hamza Bey Mosque

A 15th-century mosque with a rare colonnaded courtyard. Restoration status may affect entry in October.

Cultural route ↗
05

Rotunda

Roman, Christian and then Ottoman: its preserved minaret is a vivid marker of the city’s layered past.

Monument history ↗
06

Atatürk House

The Ottoman-era house traditionally identified as Mustafa Kemal Atatürk’s birthplace, beside the Turkish Consulate.

Check consulate notices ↗
Before you go

Practical notes

October is ideal for walking, but daylight is shorter and monument schedules can change.

Book and confirm

  • Thessaloniki–Athens train
  • Official Greek heritage tickets
  • Archaeological Museum hours
  • Thessaloniki monuments guide

Halal food strategy

  • Thessaloniki: HAYAT Mikrí Póli identifies itself as a dedicated halal Turkish restaurant; Pites tis Polis is another central Turkish option reported as halal.
  • Athens: Monastiraki has several Syrian, Lebanese, Turkish and South Asian choices; confirm the current halal status at the counter.
  • Ask whether meat is halal, alcohol is used in sauces, and pork shares the grill or fryer.
  • Vegetarian food and seafood are useful fallbacks, but still ask about wine, gelatin and shared cooking surfaces.
  • Historic Ottoman mosques in Thessaloniki are monuments, not dependable daily prayer facilities. Plan prayer separately.

Live Athens halal search ↗

Pack & pace

  • Comfortable shoes: Ano Poli has steep cobbled streets.
  • A light waterproof layer and something warmer for evenings.
  • Modest clothing for active religious sites.
  • Offline maps and a small amount of cash for markets.
  • Verify restoration access and museum closures before rearranging Friday or Saturday.
  • Departure day stays deliberately empty.
